notes: Checked: (1) the Home department landing page (/browse/home) - main nav tabs, left sidebar categories, and promotional/featured links, none labeled Bestsellers/Best Sellers/Top Sellers/Most Popular/Trending/Customer Favorites/Most Loved; (2) the Home Decor category page (/browse/home/decor) - full sub-category list and promotional banners, same result, no Bestsellers filter or link; (3) the site's full navigation-sitemap.xml (the same 10k-line/73-URL-tree source the prior Home-Decor pass used) grepped for best/popular/trend/top-rated/favorite - Nordstrom DOES expose dedicated Bestsellers PLPs elsewhere on the site (/browse/beauty/bestsellers, /browse/beauty/bestsellers/skincare, /browse/men/bestsellers, /browse/men/grooming/cologne/bestsellers, /browse/women/clothing/underwear-lingerie/bestsellers, /browse/kids/baby-gear/bestsellers, /browse/kids/shower-gifts/bestsellers, /browse/sale/bestsellers/men) confirming the site uses this exact URL/nav pattern when a Bestsellers listing exists - but none exist under /browse/home or any Home sub-category (Home Decor, Lighting & Lamps, Art Prints & Wall Decor, Mirrors, Tabletop & Dining, Vases & Planters, Picture Frames, Clocks, Candle Holders & Accessories); (4) direct probe of /browse/home/bestsellers returned no renderable content (does not resolve to a real page). Site search (/sr?keyword=...) is robots.txt-disallowed (Disallow: /sr?*, /search?*, /sr/) and returned no renderable content via WebFetch - consistent with the prior pass's access notes on this domain (ISTL interstitial). Relied on nav+sitemap+direct-URL-probe per the brief's guidance that a zero-result/blocked search is not proof of absence, but the site's own consistent exposure of Bestsellers URLs for every OTHER department, paired with their total absence for Home, is strong positive evidence of true absence rather than a discovery gap. Conclusion: no genuine Bestsellers-type PLP exists for Nordstrom Home.
